claims: The Artemis II crew successfully splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego on Friday, April 10, 2026.
The Artemis II splashdown occurred at approximately 8:07 p.m. EDT (5:07 p.m. PDT).
The Orion capsule landed safely after a 10-day mission around the Moon.
Recovery efforts for the Artemis II splashdown were led by the U.S. Navy and NASA.
Artemis II splashdown location was Pacific Ocean, near San Diego, California.
Artemis II vessel was Orion spacecraft "Integrity".
Recovery team for Artemis II was USS John P. Murtha.
Artemis II was the first crewed mission to the Moon in over 50 years.
Artemis II astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen returned safely.
